cases.sentence: Эскадрон, в котором юнкером служил Николай Ростов, расположен был в ___ Зальценек.
cases.explain: «немецкой деревне» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The Pávlograd Hussars were stationed two miles from Braunau. The squadron in which Nikoláy Rostóv served as a cadet was quartered in the German village of Salzeneck. The best quarters in the village were assigned to cavalry-captain Denísov, the squadron commander, known throughout the whole cavalry division as Váska Denísov. Cadet Rostóv, ever since he had overtaken the regiment in Poland, had lived with the squadron commander.

cases.sentence: 11 октября, в тот ___, когда в главной квартире всё было поднято на ноги известием о поражении Мака, в штабе эскадрона походная жизнь спокойно шла по-старому.
cases.explain: «самый день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On October 11, the day when all was astir at headquarters over the news of Mack’s defeat, the camp life of the officers of this squadron was proceeding as usual. Denísov, who had been losing at cards all night, had not yet come home when Rostóv rode back early in the morning from a foraging expedition. Rostóv in his cadet uniform, with a jerk to his horse, rode up to the porch, swung his leg over the saddle with a supple youthful movement, stood for a moment in the stirrup as if loathe to part from his horse, and at last sprang down and called to his orderly.

cases.sentence: Ростов в ___ подъехал к крыльцу, толконув лошадь, гибким, молодым жестом скинул ногу, постоял на стремени, как будто не желая расстаться с лошадью, наконец, спрыгнул и крикнул вестового.
cases.explain: «юнкерском мундире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

Denísov, who had been losing at cards all night, had not yet come home when Rostóv rode back early in the morning from a foraging expedition. Rostóv in his cadet uniform, with a jerk to his horse, rode up to the porch, swung his leg over the saddle with a supple youthful movement, stood for a moment in the stirrup as if loathe to part from his horse, and at last sprang down and called to his orderly.

cases.sentence: — Вы̀води, дружок, — сказал он с тою братскою, веселою нежностию, с которою обращаются со всеми хорошие ___, когда они счастливы.
cases.explain: «молодые люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, Bondarénko, dear friend!” said he to the hussar who rushed up headlong to the horse. “Walk him up and down, my dear fellow,” he continued, with that gay brotherly cordiality which goodhearted young people show to everyone when they are happy.

cases.sentence: ___ бросился тоже к лошади, но Бондаренко уже перекинул поводья трензеля.
cases.explain: «Другой гусар» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Another hussar also rushed toward the horse, but Bondarénko had already thrown the reins of the snaffle bridle over the horse’s head. It was evident that the cadet was liberal with his tips and that it paid to serve him. Rostóv patted the horse’s neck and then his flank, and lingered for a moment.

cases.sentence: Он весело улыбнулся и подмигнул: «Schön, gut Morgen! Schön, gut Morgen!»[256] ___, доброго утра! повторял он, видимо, находя удовольствие в приветствии молодого человека.
cases.explain: «Доброго утра» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Splendid! What a horse he will be!” he thought with a smile, and holding up his saber, his spurs jingling, he ran up the steps of the porch. His landlord, who in a waistcoat and a pointed cap, pitchfork in hand, was clearing manure from the cowhouse, looked out, and his face immediately brightened on seeing Rostóv. “Schön gut Morgen! Schön gut Morgen!”21 he said winking with a merry smile, evidently pleased to greet the young man.

cases.sentence: А я продулся, брат, вчера, как ___!
cases.explain: «сукин сын» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Weally! And I’ve been losing, bwother. I lost yesterday like a damned fool!” cried Denísov, not pronouncing his r’s. “Such ill luck! Such ill luck. As soon as you left, it began and went on. Hullo there! Tea!”

cases.sentence: Денисов, сморщившись, как бы улыбаясь и выказывая свои короткие ___, начал обеими руками с короткими пальцами лохматить, как лес, взбитые черные, густые волосы.
cases.explain: «крепкие зубы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Puckering up his face though smiling, and showing his short strong teeth, he began with stubby fingers of both hands to ruffle up his thick tangled black hair.
